text: Existing exact methods scale factorially with the number of streams d, while Kronecker-factorized approaches are efficient but have limited expressivity.
densityReasons: Contrasts factorial exact methods with efficient but less expressive alternatives.

text: We introduce a novel exact parameterization based on generalized orthostochastic matrices, scaling as O(d³) and exposing a hyperparameter s that interpolates between a computationally efficient boundary and the fully expressive Birkhoff polytope.
densityReasons: Combines a new construction, exactness, cubic scaling, and a tunable expressivity-efficiency range.

text: Our method composes naturally with Kronecker-factorized methods, substantially recovering expressivity at similar FLOP costs.
densityReasons: Combines composition with another method, expressivity recovery, and FLOP comparison.

text: On synthetic stream-mixing tasks, go-mHC achieves the minimum theoretical loss while converging up to 10× faster.
densityReasons: Combines task setting, theoretical optimum, and convergence-speed result.

text: The expressivity, efficiency, and exactness of go-mHC offer a practical avenue for scaling d as a new dimension of model capacity.
densityReasons: Combines three properties with a proposed scaling implication.

text: The performance and stability of modern machine learning models increasingly depend on the geometric structure of their matrix parameterizations; traditional constraints such as symmetry or orthogonality have been foundational, while recent work leverages manifold theory to map unconstrained spaces onto constrained geometries like the Birkhoff polytope, which enforces doubly stochastic constraints but faces a trade-off between exactness and scalability.
densityReasons: Compresses geometric parameterization context, manifold mapping, Birkhoff constraints, and an exactness-scalability trade-off.

text: Constraining attention patterns to doubly stochastic matrices improves accuracy in vision and language models and interprets learned parameters as probability trajectories.
densityReasons: Combines an empirical benefit and an interpretive consequence of doubly stochastic attention.

text: Sinkhorn Attention provides memory-efficient implementations due to its ability to mix internal representations and smooth optimization landscape.
densityReasons: Combines implementation efficiency, representational mixing, and optimization effects.

text: Dynamic generalizations of residual streams increase topological complexity by increasing the number of streams d while preserving the identity mapping property.
densityReasons: Combines increased stream count, topological complexity, and preservation of identity mapping.

text: Figure 1 illustrates spectral comparison showing go-mHC approximates the Birkhoff polytope within epsilon(s) error using d(d‑1)/2 parameters; mHC‑lite provides full coverage but requires d! parameters; KromHC is restricted to B₂ and disallows cycles >2. The parameterization maps skew‑symmetric X to orthogonal Q via the Cayley Transform, then projects to doubly stochastic B via block‑wise Frobenius norm. Hyper‑Connections ℋ_res is integrated into the residual stream as x_{l+1}=ℋ_l^{res} x_l + Layer F(x_l), where the doubly stochastic constraint ensures training stability and improved gradient flow.
densityReasons: Combines multiple methods, parameter counts, approximation behavior, matrix transforms, integration equations, and stability rationale.

text: Manifold‑Constrained Hyper‑Connections (mHC) shows that constraining residual connections to the interior of the Birkhoff polytope significantly improves training stability and scalability.
densityReasons: Combines a manifold constraint, Birkhoff-polytope interior, and two training benefits.

text: Exact parameterizations have been introduced to prevent error accumulation across layers (Yang and Gao 2026; Zhou et al. 2026).
densityReasons: Combines purpose, error mechanism, and cited follow-up work.

text: mHC‑lite uses the Birkhoff–von Neumann theorem to parameterize ℋ_res as a convex combination of all d! permutation matrices.
densityReasons: Combines a theorem-based method, convex-combination structure, and factorial matrix count.

text: The parameter count O(d·d!) explodes super‑exponentially; for d=8, 8! = 40 320 permutations are required, making this approach memory‑prohibitive without sampling approximations.
densityReasons: Combines asymptotic growth, a numerical example, and a memory-prohibitive consequence.

text: KromHC employs Kronecker products of small doubly stochastic matrices to achieve exact constraints with O(d²) complexity, but at the cost of severely reduced expressivity.
densityReasons: Combines construction, exactness, quadratic complexity, and expressivity trade-off.

text: The framework learns doubly stochastic matrices while balancing efficiency and expressivity, exposing a hyperparameter s that allows tunability across these attributes.
densityReasons: Combines learning objective, efficiency-expressivity trade-off, and tunability mechanism.

text: The parameterization is evaluated on a synthetic data task mixing d residual streams and a 30 M‑parameter GPT‑style language model.
densityReasons: Combines synthetic evaluation and language-model validation settings.

text: Our method achieves faster convergence and better reachability than parametrizations invoking the Birkhoff von‑Neumann theorem, such as mHC‑lite and KromHC.
densityReasons: Combines convergence and reachability comparisons against two baselines.

text: The method scales as O(d^3) in FLOP complexity and parameter count, surpassing the super‑exponential scaling of mHC‑lite and KromHC’s component factors.
densityReasons: Combines cubic FLOP and parameter scaling with two baseline comparisons.

text: The method requires no custom CUDA kernels, relying only on batched linear solves and tensor contractions.
densityReasons: Combines absence of custom kernels with two implementation techniques.

text: The method achieves exact double stochasticity by construction, with no iterations and no approximation gap.
densityReasons: Combines exactness, construction guarantee, iteration absence, and approximation-gap absence.

text: The method includes a hyperparameter s that interpolates between the orthostochastic boundary (s=1) and the dense interior of the Birkhoff polytope (s→∞).
densityReasons: Combines a tunable parameter with two limiting geometric regimes and interpolation behavior.

text: The method provides a potential avenue for scaling Hyper‑Connections with tractable complexity while maintaining significant expressivity.
densityReasons: Combines tractable complexity, expressivity preservation, and a scaling implication.

text: The method can be used simultaneously with KromHC to allow for larger Kronecker factors by mitigating the super‑exponential scaling introduced in mHC‑lite.
densityReasons: Combines simultaneous method use, larger factor support, and mitigation of factorial scaling.

text: He et al. introduced skip connections that enable gradient flow via identity shortcuts in ResNets.
densityReasons: Combines historical attribution, mechanism, and ResNet relevance.

text: Hyper‑Connections (HC) introduced the first learnable, multi‑stream generalization of residual streams allowing for dynamic mixing matrices.
densityReasons: Combines historical introduction, learnability, multi-stream structure, and dynamic mixing.

text: HC can theoretically enable models to learn depth and width connections, dynamically rearrange layer connectivity and potentially adds a new avenue for scaling.
densityReasons: Combines depth and width connectivity, dynamic rearrangement, and a scaling possibility.

text: Later works have expanded on HC by splitting the feature dimension into independent sub‑streams and applying HC to vision and graph neural networks.
densityReasons: Combines feature partitioning with applications to two neural-network domains.

text: The unconstrained dynamic connectivity of residual blocks in HC removes the explicit guarantee of the identity property, introducing the risk of gradient instability after repeated applications of the mixing terms.
densityReasons: Combines unconstrained connectivity, loss of identity guarantees, repeated mixing, and instability risk.

text: Subsequent works investigate constraining this connectivity to a manifold that bounds gradient updates through the spectral norm in order to address this instability.
densityReasons: Combines later work, manifold constraints, spectral-norm bounding, and the instability target.

text: Manifold‑Constrained Hyper‑Connections (mHC) constrain the dynamic residual matrices to a manifold to improve training stability while still allowing for dynamic connections.
densityReasons: Combines constrained residual matrices, manifold structure, stability, and dynamic connectivity.

text: mHC primarily changes the definition of ℋ_l^res such that it converges to the Birkhoff polytope B_d, the closed set of doubly stochastic matrices.
densityReasons: Combines a definition change, convergence behavior, and the Birkhoff-polytope target.

text: B_d denotes the closed set of doubly stochastic matrices, defined as positive matrices with the property M^T J_d = M J_d = J_d.
densityReasons: Combines set identification, positivity, two matrix equations, and notation for doubly stochasticity.

text: mHC‑lite attempts to circumvent the approximation gap and customized kernel by making use of the Birkhoff–von Neumann theorem to define the learned connections as a convex combination of d! permutation matrices.
densityReasons: Combines the motivation, theorem, parameterization strategy, and factorial-sized representation.

text: KromHC sacrifices expressivity and complete coverage of B_d by using tensor products to train residual connections on a much smaller set of exactly double‑stochastic matrices, with a cost of O(d² C).
densityReasons: Combines expressivity loss, coverage loss, tensor-product construction, exactness, matrix-set restriction, and complexity.

text: Comparisons with the matrix exponential show similar quality and better stability at lower FLOP cost.
densityReasons: Combines comparative quality, stability, and computational-cost findings.

densityReasons: Combines containment, spanning, a parameterized matrix family, and an asymptotic limit.

text: To our knowledge, we are the first to apply this construction in a machine learning setting and, more specifically, to learned residual stream routing in deep networks.
densityReasons: Combines a novelty claim, construction, machine-learning setting, and specific routing application.
